objective: Combine the fixed-triangle packing theorem with C18 to derive the weaker integer bound B(n)+o(n^2), narrow integer near-extremizers to the low-core dual branch, and calibrate linear rounding gaps.

atomic_claims.text: All chordal G have cp(G)<=B(n)+2a(n), where the general triangle-packing gap a(n)=o(n^2); the chordal and split integer extrema divided by n^2 both tend to 1/6.
Any asymptotically integer-extremal chordal sequence eventually has low-core compression with r=n/3+o(n), P=o(n), and R+D=o(n^2).
The K4 windmill on n=3k+1 vertices has nu_star-nu=k=(n-1)/3, but cp=k, so it calibrates rounding loss without threatening the root.

assumptions: Finite simple graphs and edge-disjoint triangle packings.
The fixed-triangle Haxell-Rodl/Yuster theorem in the explicit uniform epsilon form; isolated vertices are handled in the candidate.
C18 fractional extremum and exact packing identities; C19 compression branch estimates; C01 attained split benchmark.

risks: The integer conclusion has o(n^2), not O(n), remainder and does not close the root or exact domination target.
